record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Is every nuclear F-space a Montel space, meaning that every bounded subset is compact?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 12. - Is each nuclear space a Montel space ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\tau)$ be an F-space, that is, a topological vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$) whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric (local convexity is not assumed). A subset $B\subset X$ is bounded if for every neighborhood $U$ of $0$ there exists $t>0$ with $B\subset tU$. Call $X$ a Montel space if every bounded closed subset of $X$ is compact.

A nuclear F-space is defined as follows. For an F-seminorm (or, equivalently, a sequence of F-seminorms generating the topology) $\|\cdot\|$ on $X$, a continuous linear operator $T:X\to Y$ between F-spaces is nuclear if it admits a representation
$$T(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n\, f_n(x)\, y_n,$$
where $(f_n)$ is an equicontinuous sequence in the dual of $X$, $(y_n)$ is a bounded sequence in $Y$, and $(\lambda_n)\in\ell^1$. The F-space $X$ is called nuclear if for every continuous F-seminorm $p$ on $X$ there exists a continuous F-seminorm $q\ge p$ such that the canonical map $X_q\to X_p$ between the associated quotient/completion spaces is nuclear.

Question: Is every nuclear F-space a Montel space?
artifact.status_search_result: In the locally convex setting it is classical that every nuclear Fréchet space is Montel. For nuclear F-spaces without the local convexity assumption, the literature located in the search does not provide a definitive answer, and the problem appears in collections of open problems on metric linear spaces without a verified resolution.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Every nuclear Fréchet space is a Montel space; in particular it is reflexive.
status_evidence.claim: Result is known in the locally convex Fréchet setting, but this does not settle the non-locally-convex F-space case.

status_evidence.title: Montel space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A barrelled quasi-complete nuclear space is a Montel space.
status_evidence.claim: Standard result requires local convexity/barrelledness; does not apply directly to general nuclear F-spaces.
